units.translation: c. 〈ῥυόμεναι:〉 guarding around and owing to save. Lᵐ
d. ῥυσέμεναι instead of σώσειν. P
e. κείνη γὰρ ἐναίσιμος: for that voyage of yours is auspicious and fitting, the one through the Wandering Rocks. L
f. ἐναίσιμος means fitting and proper. P
862-65. ἀλλὰ σὺ μή τῳ ἐμὸν δ〈είξῃς〉: do not show me to any of the Argo-
nauts, whenever you see me with the Nereids coming to meet you. L
864. ἀπηλεγέως: unambiguously. Lᴳ P
865-66. ἀΐδηλος ἐδύ〈σατο〉: becoming invisible she sank into the depth of the sea. And grief struck Peleus terribly. L
868a. 〈νηπιάχοντος:〉 being an infant and thinking infantile thoughts. Lᴳ
b. νηπιάχειν means νηπιάζειν. P
871a. ἀμβροσίῃ χρίεσκεν: with most divine oil she anointed his tender body. L
b. ἀμβροσίαν means ambrosial oil. P
872a. καί οἱ στυγερὸν χροΐ: and to him. May she drive hateful old age from his body. L
b. ἀλάλκειν means to cast out. P
874. σπαίροντα διὰ φλογός: leaping and tossing on the fire.
876. τὸν μὲν ἄρ’ ἁρπάγδην: snatching him from the fire she threw him on the ground screaming. L
879-80a. παλίσσυτος: after this she no longer came back to Peleus; hence neglect bound his mind. L
b. ἀμηχανία means helplessness and grief. P
884. τῆς ἔνι δαισάμε〈νοι〉: feasting and dining on these they slept the night as before, that is, as on another night. L
886a. 〈κατηλυσίῃ:〉 descent. Lᴳ
b. κατηλυσία means descent and arrival. P
887-89a. βαῖνον ἐπὶ κληῖδ〈ας〉: they went up onto the planks of the ship and their own seats.
b. ἐκ δὲ βυθοῖο εὐναίας: from the depths they brought up or
hauled up the anchors, rejoicing at the coming of the west wind, and they piled up and prepared the rigging as was necessary.
890a. τανύσαντες ἐν ἱμά〈ντεσσι〉: stretching the yardarm with the straps and raising it with the sail. L
b. He means the straps of the yardarm, with which the sail is fastened to the yardarm. P

892. καλὴν Ἀνθεμόεσσαν: he followed Hesiod, who names the island of the Sirens thus (fr. 68 Rz.²): ‘to the island Anthemoessa, where the son of Cronus gave it to them.’ Their names are Thelxiope or Thelxinoe, Molpe, Aglaophonus.
897. 〈ἀδμῆτ’ ἔτι〉 πορσύνεσκον: they delighted, deemed worthy of care, and raised her while still a maiden and unyoked. Lᵐ (P)

900-02. 〈αἰεὶ δ’ εὐόρμου:〉 always looking around and observing from the high and well-anchored place, they snatched the sweet return of many passers-by, causing them to waste away with melting. Lᵐ (P)
907a. 〈ἐυτροχάλοιο:〉 she stirred the melody of the well-rounded song. Lᵐ
b. εὐτρόχαλος means flowing easily, smoothly, and tunefully. P
c. κανάχησε means sang and stirred. P
909. κρεγμῷ: with the striking, by the strumming.
